questions.def: Use 'much' with uncountable nouns like 'money' in negative sentences.
questions.question: I don't have ___ money to buy that car.

questions.def: 'Fewer' is used with countable nouns like 'people'.
questions.question: ___ people came to the party than we expected.

questions.def: 'Eat' is the base form after 'did not'.
questions.question: He didn't ___ much for breakfast.

questions.def: 'Few' means almost none, suitable for countable nouns.
questions.question: She has ___ friends in her new city.

questions.def: 'Any' is typically used in questions.
questions.question: Do you need ___ help with your homework?

questions.def: 'Want' is the base form after 'don't'.
questions.question: I don't ___ much sugar in my coffee.

questions.def: 'Much' is used with uncountable nouns like 'milk' in negatives.
questions.question: There isn't ___ milk in the fridge.

questions.def: 'Little' is used with uncountable nouns like 'time'.
questions.question: I have ___ time to finish this project.

questions.def: 'Much' not 'many' is used for uncountable nouns (water).
questions.question: She has many water in her bottle now.

questions.def: 'Did' is needed to form a question with 'many' in the past simple.
questions.question: ___ many people to the concert yesterday?

questions.def: 'Most' is used as a quantifier to indicate a majority.
questions.question: ___ of the students passed the exam.

questions.def: 'A lot of' is used with both countable and uncountable nouns.
questions.question: She has ___ experience in this field.

questions.def: 'Have' is the base form after 'don't'.
questions.question: They don't ___ much free time.

questions.def: 'A few' is used with countable nouns, meaning some but not many.
questions.question: We need ___ more chairs for the guests.

questions.def: 'Most' refers to the largest part of something.
questions.question: ___ of the cake was eaten.

questions.def: 'Much' is correct with uncountable nouns like 'information'.
questions.question: There is many information available online today.

questions.def: 'Are' is correct with plural nouns like 'options'.
questions.question: There ___ not many options left.

questions.def: 'Some' indicates a portion of a group.
questions.question: ___ of my friends live in this city.

questions.def: 'More' can be used for both countable and uncountable nouns.
questions.question: I have ___ apples than you do.

questions.def: 'Little' is correct with uncountable nouns like 'water'.
questions.question: She drank few water after running the race.

questions.def: 'Many' is correct because students are countable.
questions.question: How ___ students in the class?

questions.def: 'Any' is typically used in negative statements.
questions.question: I don't have ___ siblings.

questions.def: 'All' means the entire quantity.
questions.question: ___ of the food was delicious.

questions.def: 'Need' is the base form after 'don't'.
questions.question: I don't ___ much help.

questions.def: 'More' is used to compare quantities of countable nouns.
questions.question: She has ___ books than I do.

questions.def: 'Half' is a fraction that can quantify pizza.
questions.question: He ate ___ of the pizza.

questions.def: Use 'much' with uncountable nouns like money in negative sentences.
questions.question: I don't have ___ money to buy that car.

questions.def: 'A lot of' is used with countable nouns like people.
questions.question: There are ___ people in the park today.

questions.def: Use 'Many' before countable nouns like students.
questions.question: Much students like to study online.

questions.def: 'Little' is used with uncountable nouns like milk.
questions.question: There is very ___ milk left in the fridge.
